meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Owen saw a zero on his phone in class. Was he heard before that?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. You haven't answered me, though: did anyone talk to Owen first?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, I'm writing that down. He wrote it over the weekend and pasted it in. And you still haven't told me whether anyone heard him before that zero went in.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Then pull it up, Hale. I'll read it myself.
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Seventeen-year-olds misremember Shakespeare all the time. And that screen is still facing you.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
So he changed his mind in two weeks, which is what an outline is for. You keep describing things; put the version history on paper in front of me.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
So he was heard, the day before. Owen tells me you've had it in for him since September, so a note in your own hand is your word against his.
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in a classroom against a weekend at home; of course they don't look alike. You've described a great deal, Hale, and handed me nothing.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Then why bring it into the room at all? The company that sells that checker says it can't be the sole basis, and so does 4.3.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
That's 4.4, and I'll want it in writing tonight. Nothing on his record, nothing in front of his class, and I still haven't seen one page of what you've got.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Ten minutes. Not until those pages are on this desk where I can read them.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
A date is not a document, Hale. Pages first.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
No. Nothing's agreed while your evidence is still sitting on your side of the desk.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
You know exactly what I need. Without it, I go from this room to the principal's office.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Cc: Principal

In today's meeting you committed to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, not in front of Owen's class, with the new mark replacing the zero and a written promise that nothing goes on his record. I still expect to read every document you described for myself, and I want the zero withdrawn. I expect that commitment from you in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Fallback position; she still wants to read your documents with her own eyes and wants the zero off and nothing on Owen's record, and she never accepted the rewrite, even though a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4 is the fair outcome and she had time left to reach it.
What moved her: You put procedure 4.4 on the table as private, off his record and in writing, which met the one thing she would never give up.
What cost ground: You described six pieces of evidence but never turned the screen or handed her a page, so none of it counted as shown and she could not accept a deal while still asking to see it.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the writing between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on the Wednesday night before it was due, right on top of that kind of late October night; that proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she told you to pull up the version history, turn the screen right then and walk her through the times before moving on to the misquoted line.
